# 1 Kings Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Much later, in the third year of the drought, the LORD said to Elijah, "Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain."
**2** So Elijah set out to see Ahab. The famine in Samaria was desperate by now.
**3** Ahab had summoned Obadiah, his palace administrator. Obadiah was a deeply devout man —
**4** when Jezebel was slaughtering the LORD's prophets, Obadiah had hidden a hundred of them in two caves, fifty in each, and had kept them alive with food and water.
**5** Ahab told Obadiah, "Let's go through the whole country, checking every spring and valley. Maybe we can find enough grass to keep the horses and mules alive so we don't have to start killing livestock."
**6** They split up the territory between them. Ahab went one direction; Obadiah went another.
**7** As Obadiah was walking along, Elijah suddenly appeared. Obadiah recognized him, fell face down, and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"
**8** "It is," Elijah answered. "Go tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"
**9** "What have I done wrong," Obadiah protested, "that you would send me to my death?
**10** I swear by the LORD your God, there's not a nation or kingdom where Ahab hasn't sent people looking for you. When they said you weren't there, he made them swear under oath that they couldn't find you.
**11** And now you tell me to go say, 'Elijah is here'?
**12** As soon as I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD will whisk you away to who knows where. When I tell Ahab and he can't find you, he'll kill me! And I've been faithful to the LORD since I was young.
**13** Hasn't my lord been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets? I hid a hundred of them in caves — fifty to a cave — and kept them supplied with food and water.
**14** And now you say, 'Go tell your master Elijah is here.' He'll kill me!"
**15** Elijah said, "As the LORD Almighty lives — the God I serve — I will present myself to Ahab today."
**16** So Obadiah went to find Ahab and delivered the message. Ahab came to meet Elijah.
**17** When Ahab saw him, he said, "So there you are — the man who has brought disaster on Israel!"
**18** "I haven't brought disaster on Israel," Elijah shot back. "You have — you and your father's family — by abandoning the LORD's commands and following the Baals.
**19** Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."
**20** So Ahab sent word throughout Israel and assembled the prophets on Mount Carmel.
**21** Elijah stood before all the people and said, "How long are you going to waver between two options? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is God, follow him." The people said nothing.
**22** Then Elijah said, "I am the only prophet of the LORD still standing. Baal has four hundred and fifty.
**23** Bring us two bulls. Let the prophets of Baal choose one, butcher it, and lay it on the wood — but don't light the fire. I'll prepare the other bull the same way.
**24** Then you call on your god, and I'll call on the LORD. The god who answers with fire — he is the real God." All the people agreed: "That's a fair test."
**25** Elijah told the prophets of Baal, "You go first since there are so many of you. Choose your bull, prepare it, and call on your god. But do not light the fire."
**26** They took the bull, prepared it, and called on Baal from morning till noon: "Baal! Answer us!" But there was no response. No one answered. They danced around the altar they had built.
**27** At noon Elijah began taunting them: "Shout louder! After all, he's a god! Maybe he's deep in thought, or busy, or traveling. Maybe he's fallen asleep and needs to be woken up!"
**28** So they shouted louder and slashed themselves with swords and spears, as was their practice, until their blood flowed.
**29** The afternoon wore on, and they continued their frantic prophesying until the time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no response. No answer. No sign of attention.
**30** Then Elijah called to all the people, "Come closer." They came. He repaired the LORD's altar, which had been torn down.
**31** Elijah took twelve stones — one for each tribe descended from Jacob, the man God renamed Israel.
**32** With these stones he rebuilt the altar in the name of the LORD. He dug a trench around it large enough to hold about twenty-five pounds of seed.
**33** He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and laid it on the wood. Then he said, "Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the offering and the wood."
**34** "Do it again," he said, and they did. "Do it a third time," he said, and they did.
**35** The water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.
**36** At the time of the evening sacrifice, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and prayed: "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, prove today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant and have done all this at your command.
**37** Answer me, LORD! Answer me! Let these people know that you, LORD, are God, and that you are winning their hearts back."
**38** The fire of the LORD fell. It burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, the soil — and licked up all the water in the trench.
**39** When all the people saw it, they threw themselves facedown on the ground and cried, "The LORD — he is God! The LORD — he is God!"
**40** Elijah ordered, "Seize the prophets of Baal! Don't let a single one escape!" They seized them, and Elijah had them brought down to the Kishon Valley, where he executed them.
**41** Then Elijah told Ahab, "Go eat and drink. I can hear the sound of heavy rain coming."
**42** So Ahab went to eat and drink. But Elijah climbed to the summit of Carmel, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.
**43** He said to his servant, "Go and look toward the sea." The servant went, looked, and came back: "Nothing." Seven times Elijah said, "Go back."
**44** The seventh time, the servant reported, "There's a cloud rising from the sea — tiny, about the size of a man's fist." Elijah said, "Go tell Ahab, 'Hitch up your chariot and get down the mountain before the rain traps you.'"
**45** In no time the sky turned black with storm clouds and wind, and a torrential rain began. Ahab rode off toward Jezreel.
**46** The power of the LORD came on Elijah. He tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **18:21 — "How long are you going to waver?"**: Elijah's challenge is not "choose God" — it's "stop standing in the middle." Israel's sin isn't atheism; it's hedge-betting. They want YHWH and Baal. Elijah says: that's not an option. Choose.
2. **18:27 — the taunt**: Elijah's mockery is the most devastating satire in the Bible. He suggests Baal might be meditating, relieving himself, or napping. It's crude, funny, and lethal — because the best argument against a false god is to make him look ridiculous.
3. **18:34 — the water**: Elijah drenches his sacrifice three times before calling for fire. He is not making the test fair — he is making it impossible. The more impossible it is, the more unmistakable the answer will be.
4. **18:38 — everything burns**: The fire doesn't just consume the bull. It consumes the wood, the stones, the dirt, and the water. This is not lightning. This is the undeniable, overwhelming, consuming presence of God.
5. **18:46 — Elijah outruns a chariot**: Seventeen miles from Carmel to Jezreel, on foot, ahead of a royal chariot in a rainstorm. The "hand of the LORD" enables what is physically impossible. This is the apex of Elijah's power — and the next chapter will show its collapse.

— PNEUMA
